title: A Structural and ac Conductivity Study on Li Doped ZnO
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In the present work, the incorporation of
                    <jats:italic>Li</jats:italic>
                    in a wurtzite ZnO host synthesized through a chemical route has been studied experimentally. Starting with Yoshio’s model, [K. Yoshio, A. Onodera, H. Satoh, N. Sakagami and H. Yamashita,
                    <jats:italic>Ferroelectrics</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:bold>264</jats:bold>
                    , 133 (2001)] structural refinement of the powder diffraction data suggests that
                    <jats:italic>Li</jats:italic>
                    has a mixed occupancy at both the substitutional 2
                    <jats:italic>b</jats:italic>
                    (≈1.2%) and interstitial 2
                    <jats:italic>a</jats:italic>
                    (≈12.6%) Wykoff sites. In comparison with a pure ZnO sample, the net result appears to be an overall expansion of the unit cell by ∼0.07% along both
                    <jats:italic>
                      <jats:bold>a</jats:bold>
                    </jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>
                      <jats:bold>c</jats:bold>
                    </jats:italic>
                    -axes. Temperature dependant
                    <jats:italic>ac</jats:italic>
                    conductivity measurements carried out using a two electrode assembly and the influence of superimposed
                    <jats:italic>dc</jats:italic>
                    bias suggest that the conduction may be governed by both the presence of interstitial
                    <jats:italic>Li</jats:italic>
                    and polar defect complexes also. The grains seem to respond more to an applied
                    <jats:italic>dc</jats:italic>
                    bias (an order of magnitude change in resistivity) than grain boundaries.
                  </jats:p>
journal: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology
